rules.title: California Civil Code section 1946.2 (Tenant Protection Act just cause)
rules.requirement: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months, the owner may not terminate the tenancy without just cause stated in the written notice. No-fault terminations require relocation assistance or a final-month rent waiver equal to one month's rent, and a non-compliant notice is void.
rules.key_value: Just cause required after 12 months of occupancy; no-fault relocation equals one month's rent, paid within 15 calendar days of notice
rules.penalty: Notice is void; owner is liable for actual damages, attorney's fees and costs, and up to three times actual damages for willful or malicious violations; injunctive relief by the Attorney General, city attorney or county counsel
rules.status_basis: Section appears in the California Civil Code; the text references July 1, 2020 and July 1, 2022 dates but does not state the act's own enactment or effective date.

exempt_if.text: Housing that has been issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, unless the housing is a mobilehome.
Residential real property that is alienable separate from the title to any other dwelling unit

exempt_if.name: owner_not_REIT_corporation_or_LLC_with_corporate_member_and_exemption_notice_given
exempt_if.text: Owner is not a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member, and tenants were given written exemption notice
Two separate dwelling units within a single structure

exempt_if.name: owner_occupied
exempt_if.text: Owner occupied one of the units as principal residence at the beginning of the tenancy and continues in occupancy
Single-family owner-occupied residences renting no more than two units or bedrooms

exempt_if.name: special_housing
exempt_if.text: Transient and tourist hotels; nonprofit hospital, religious facility, extended care or licensed care facilities; dormitories; housing sharing bathroom or kitchen with the owner; deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing

coverage.exemptions_summary: Exempts transient hotels, care facilities, dormitories, owner-shared housing, owner-occupied single-family and duplex properties, housing with a certificate of occupancy within 15 years, separately alienable homes with non-corporate owners, and deed-restricted affordable housing.

precedence.text: This section does not apply to residential real property subject to a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before September 1, 2019, or adopted or amended after that date that is more protective than this section, in which case the local ordinance shall apply.

rules.quoted_span: (a) Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
